L1: the forms become one shared, cached set

# GET /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
# Prefer: forms=link
# 200 OK
# ETag: "seq-1.hsf.L1"
# Cache-Control: no-cache
# Preference-Applied: forms=link
clientCertificateId: xmbiqp
createdDate: 2015-12-08T18:02:16Z
description: test-client-cert-2
expirationDate: 2016-12-07T18:02:16Z
pemEncodedCertificate: |
  -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- …
_links:
  self:
    href: /clientcertificates/xmbiqp
  hr:forms:
    href: /affordance-sets/{hash}
    type: application/hal+json
    profile: https://w3id.org/heart-rise/
      hal-schema-forms
    integrity: sha256-…
# GET /affordance-sets/{hash}
# Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
_forms:
  clientcertificate:update:
    title: Update
    _links:
      target:
        href: /clientcertificates/{id}
        templated: true
    hr:templatePointers:
      id: /clientCertificateId
    method: PATCH
    contentType: application/json
    hr:integrity: sha256-…
    schema:
      type: object
      required: [patchOperations]
      properties:
        patchOperations: {…as at L0…}
  clientcertificate:delete:
    title: Delete
    _links:
      target:
        href: /clientcertificates/{id}
        templated: true
    hr:templatePointers:
      id: /clientCertificateId
    method: DELETE

MOCKUP Today L0 L1 L2 One set for every certificate: fetched once, then read from cache.
say: Mockup. With Prefer: forms=link, the certificate links its form set instead of inlining it. Every certificate links the same set, at a content address with an integrity hash, cached for a year and immutable. The target becomes a template the client fills from the certificate's own state, by the pointer. The certificate itself is still revalidated by its ETag; a state seen before costs one 304.
